text:
Casey Mittelstadt has become a different player in Boston, and Boston Hockey Now put it plainly: he's embracing a shutdown role. For a center long known as an offensive talent who didn't defend enough, that's quite a turn. He has also been scoring, with 8 goals and 14 points in 22 games on about 14 minutes a night, and his name is turning up in trade pitches (Yahoo Sports floated him as the centerpiece of a package for Dylan Larkin).

Here's the catch. His 8 goals have come on 4.6 expected, a 27% shooting rate, and Boston has scored 7.2 more goals than expected with him on the ice. The chances are real. That finishing rate rarely lasts. The more durable news is at five on five, where the Bruins get about 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, even while being outshot in attempts.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a setup man last season, 81st percentile among forwards. He's fast and his shot is soft, so his goals come from getting to good ice. We'd watch whether the defensive role sticks once the shooting cools.
